content:
R265 — Free SYCL native prefill grouped FP16 GEMM optimization candidates
Date: 2026-10-12
Status: read-only source research; no build, execution, test, GPU/process query, profiler, Git action, or source edit. No new performance claim or B570 dispatch result is made.

Scope and source identity
Target is WN integrated source HEAD `0691bcdf5af63a85b3b25650f367d3276db64035` in `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/sync-xe-v0143-nonfinite-20261012`. The intended device is Intel Arc B570 and workload one 8,192-token prefill chunk. `STRATA_ONEMATH=0` compiles `Gemm::f16_groups` as an unconditional `return false` (`src/prefill/gemm.cpp:343-360`), so the grouped calls fall through to `xmx_gemm_grouped`; the backend that this later chooses is runtime-dependent and is not established by this source review. R262 independently covers exact event-timing rules; this report focuses on optimization opportunities and selection experiments.

SHA-256 of reviewed source:
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: `2922806c8b56b64e1bc20096d93c852a105ed225ff3bf9dcf113436c79964d9c`
- `src/prefill/gemm.cpp`: `bfa40846fddb46a3d03d8c58ef5209b181c46674939beeefe512db0073c9d648`
- `src/prefill/kernels.cpp`: `0e89bbb83220ad85257d17fc6b98f2332a5c17e8d2832937a98a1e3ae300ab81`
- `src/kernels/xe/xmx_gemm.cpp`: `2d2144e7331b3dd66a2289a9c67b541b1c136332be53f31c935c9176880085d1`
- `src/kernels/xe/mma_gemm.cpp`: `540a4366709b8a2caf43aae36bbaeefd21bf4290d5555557077c463754da2238`
- `src/kernels/xe/dp4a_gemm.cpp`: `3d6b98f7294e0ae2b7aa497fbf701d54dce799ca8970fae02fcf37ff852587bf`
- `src/core/device.cpp`: `3e7523a2947af7c82d41fc9a7653f4f9aad0fa3cbb062999de19553659e0ec27`

Actual grouped shapes and execution geometry
`prefill.cpp:1924-2023` counts routes per expert from the current top-k IDs, sorts/selects any CPU-served routes, and places GPU routes before CPU routes. `rows_gpu` is `T*K - rows_cpu`. No fixed per-expert count follows from the source. For `T=8192`, `K=8`, there are 65,536 total routed entries before CPU offload; the actual GPU row count can be lower. At most 512 expert IDs are available. `m.cnt[e]` is variable and bounds are built from those exact counts.

For the ordinary free grouped-FP16 fallback, `fallback_products` (`prefill.cpp:2185-2225`) processes experts in groups of `g_expert_group` (default 16, setter clamps 1–64 at lines 1060-1061). It computes the actual group's `maxr` and `G`, then launches GU and down. GU has output width N=1280 (interleaved gate/up, 640 values each) and reduction K=H=2560; down has N=H=2560 and K=FF=640. Route bounds identify the variable row intervals. In compact mode, groups can be further partitioned by `compact_moe_groups` and use each group's actual `max_rows` (`2186-2209`). The separate resident IQ fused-dequant kernel route is not this FP16 grouped GEMM.

`xmx_gemm_grouped` uses WM=128, WN=256, PD=3 (`xmx_gemm.cpp:321-339`). Its internal joint-matrix tile is TM=8,TN=16,TK=16; each 16-lane subgroup computes a 32x64 output strip from 4x4 joint-matrix accumulators, and a work-group comprises 16 such subgroups (256 work-items) (`36-39`, `81-105`, `137-178`). K is staged in KC=32 increments. Thus one kernel command covers 80 outer KC steps for GU K=2560 and 20 for down K=640. N=1280 GU requires five 256-column tiles, and N=2560 down requires ten. The global M grid uses `ceil(maxr/128)` for every expert in the call; `GroupedKernel` checks each expert's own bounds and returns from any extra M tile (`xmx_gemm.cpp:164-175`).

X and W are not independently transposed into a new layout by this XMX kernel. The source stores row-major FP16 expert matrices; the XMX tile reads W in a column-major joint-matrix view at the selected expert's base (`xmx_gemm.cpp:77-105`, 172-175). Each subgroup reuses loaded A fragments across several N tiles and B fragments across several M tiles. A candidate should retain this reuse, the grouped bounds, and the current F32 accumulators unless measurements justify a change.

Ranked source-backed candidates

1. Fuse the grouped GU SwiGLU conversion into the XMX GU output epilogue.

Current fallback writes `G`'s 1280 FP32 outputs per route row to `m.GU`, then launches `swiglu_interleaved`, which reads the gate/up pair and writes 640 saturated FP16 values to `m.Hh` (`prefill.cpp:2218-2224`; `kernels.cpp:970-977`). A grouped-XMX-specific epilogue can consume even/odd output columns as gate/up, compute `hf_sat(g/(1+exp(-g))*u)` and write only the existing `Hh` FP16 result. The current group tile has 16 even columns, so pair boundaries fit inside each TN=16 output tile, although accumulator-fragment extraction/store and partial-row handling need careful implementation. A local staging tile or explicit lane mapping may be needed to apply the epilogue to joint-matrix results; do not assume the fragment is directly indexable.

Conditional byte accounting: baseline GU writes 1280 FP32 = 5,120 bytes/route, and the separate SwiGLU reads those 5,120 bytes; both paths still write the final 640 FP16 = 1,280 bytes/route. Therefore, if all 65,536 routes are GPU-served, the upper-bound global intermediate traffic removable for one layer is 2*5,120*65,536 = 671,088,640 bytes (640 MiB). For `rows_gpu` GPU routes, scale the expression to `10,240*rows_gpu`; this is logical traffic, not a measured DRAM amount. It also removes one kernel launch. Actual bandwidth/time benefit is unknown and may be limited by epilogue conversion cost or fragment movement.

Selection evidence: make a narrow output-parity fixture from exact grouped FP16 operands/bounds. Compare all GU-derived Hh elements against current `swiglu_interleaved` (FP32 inputs, same sigmoid expression, same saturating FP16 conversion), including uneven expert row counts, last-row/last-tile tails, positive/negative/extreme finite values, zeros, and the existing non-finite gate. Then compare grouped GU device duration and the pair of GU+SwiGLU commands against the fused command, and check the quiet full 8K prefill endpoint. Accept only if numerical gates pass and matched repeats show an endpoint win. Keep the current separate route for all unsupported backends and failures.

2. Remove the materialized gathered Xs plane for grouped GU by staging source-indexed activation tiles directly.

Before fallback GEMM, `gather_rows16` copies each activation row selected by `src_dev` into expert-contiguous `Xs` (`prefill.cpp:2120-2126`, implementation `kernels.cpp:985-994`); the grouped GEMM then reads Xs as regular contiguous rows. With H=2560 FP16, this intermediate is 5,120 bytes per routed row. The existing path logically reads each source row for gather, writes the Xs copy, and reads that copy for GU. A fused input path could use the existing expert-ordered row-to-token `src_dev` map to copy the requested activation K tile into a work-group local tile immediately before `joint_matrix_load`. At `KC=32`, a 128-row activation tile is only 8 KiB of FP16 source values. It could eliminate the global Xs write and subsequent Xs read and remove the standalone gather launch; the unavoidable activation reads remain. For all 65,536 GPU rows the upper-bound logical intermediate avoided is again `2*5120*65536 = 640 MiB` per layer; use actual `rows_gpu` for the route. The compact path already gathers each compact sub-group, so it needs the same direct indexed tile design with its group-relative row map. This change affects A-tile loading/layout and is higher implementation risk than the output epilogue: source token IDs can be irregular, and the local staging must preserve coalesced loads, alignment, synchronization, joint-matrix legality, and register/SLM occupancy.

Selection evidence: first compare the direct-index A staging against the current gathered Xs route on the same bounds and raw FP16 data, testing varied token IDs, duplicate token IDs across experts, compact and ordinary group boundaries, H-tail/alignment cases permitted by `xmx_gemm_ok`, and exact CPU/reference output tolerances. Measure the gather command separately from grouped GU, then compare their sum with the direct-index grouped command and the quiet 8K prefill endpoint. Report local-memory use and occupancy/spill evidence for the new exact kernel. Only retain it if launch plus transfer savings exceed any irregular-load cost and all route outputs pass.

3. Specialize M tiling or compact the grouped M work list using observed per-expert counts.

The fixed launch uses `G*ceil(maxr/128)*nN` work-groups; each one has 16 subgroups. For a given expert with `c_e < maxr`, high M tiles with `tm*128 >= c_e` return without doing GEMM work. A source-informed schedule can build a compact descriptor over actual experts and their valid `ceil(c_e/WM)` M tiles, so the kernel launches `sum_e ceil(c_e/WM)*nN` work-groups rather than `G*ceil(maxr/WM)*nN`, while preserving actual `bounds`. Another, simpler variant can dispatch a WM=64 (or 32) tile for small-maximum groups to reduce row-tail padding. These choices must be based on a retained histogram of actual `m.cnt` values and `maxr` per launched fallback group; the global average 65,536/512 is not a per-expert assumption and is not a dispatch criterion. At N widths in this workload there is no WN tail (`1280` and `2560` are multiples of 256), so prioritize M rather than WN retuning. Smaller WM can increase number of work-groups and weaken A reuse; descriptor compaction reduces no-op blocks but adds descriptor construction/indexing.

Selection evidence: record per invocation `G`, maxr, every `c_e` or a lossless count histogram, `ceil(maxr/128)`, and the exact number of no-op M tiles. Replay a representative set of real grouped bound arrays at GU and down shapes. Compare 128/64/32 variants and compact descriptors using the same operands; report active vs launched work-groups, direct grouped-event duration, correctness, and the quiet endpoint. Keep WM=128 when tails are rare or smaller tiles worsen throughput. The existing group size (16 by default) is a separate axis; do not expand it in the same first comparison because that changes dequant scratch and maxr distributions.

B570 eligibility and safe fallback
The current selector (`xmx_gemm.cpp:207-255, 316-339`) uses the grouped XMX kernel only if runtime-reported subgroups include 16, the reported joint-matrix combination supports FP16 A/B, FP32 accumulator/output, and an 8x16x16 tile, the large-GRF kernel bundle probe succeeds, and XMX was not disabled. It otherwise goes to the existing MMA or DP4a branch according to `mma_usable` and `mma_forced`; `xmx_gemm_ok` additionally enforces N>=16, N%16=0, K>=32, K%32=0, 64-byte pointer alignment, output stride alignment, and grouped W-stride alignment (`280-282`, `319-320`). For this model's N/K shapes these dimension tests are satisfied by construction, but this does not prove the installed B570 stack selects XMX.

Any new specialization must not key on the string “B570” alone. Retain matrix-combination and 16-subgroup checks; compile/query the exact executable bundle for the precise new `GroupedKernel<WM,WN,PD,...>` specialization before dispatch, since the existing GRF probe instantiates a non-grouped `GemmKernel<half,128,256,3>` (`228-238`) and does not prove a new grouped specialization is buildable. If any check fails, use the unchanged existing grouped XMX kernel when it is already eligible, or the current MMA/DP4a fallback as its existing selector dictates; never force the unsupported variant. Keep exact existing FP32 accumulation and output if a lower-precision result path has not separately passed quality qualification.

Measurement sequence that chooses among candidates
1. Use one fresh 8K input/model/settings recipe and capture the actual GPU-route bounds/counts for each tested layer; keep CPU offload, resident cache, expert group, MMQ/fused/native-dequant flags, and stream/ring settings fixed. A route receipt must identify the runtime-selected grouped backend so XMX-specific outcomes are not attributed to a fallback. Keep the actual count arrays, not a uniform synthetic average.
2. For each candidate, run its narrow component parity check first. Use exact grouped event duration for the commands under test where the profiling-queue diagnostic is valid, plus host submission/completion and quiet-production measurements as separate numbers. If event timing cannot be queried, retain it as unavailable rather than substituting phase markers. This follows the already reviewed R262 contract without revisiting its design.
3. Measure candidate and baseline in matched order, same queue/device/affinity and identical activation/weights/bounds. For input/epilogue fusion, compare removed command plus grouped GEMM against new fused command. For tiling, compare direct event time and active/launched workgroups on the same count arrays. Finally compare repeated quiet full-8K prefill times and required output/logit parity. Do not infer full-model benefit from kernel-only service time.
4. Introduce one optimization at a time. If a kernel-level gain does not survive the prefill endpoint, do not adopt it. Preserve baseline/fallback dispatch and source-only status until the exact B570 build and numerical/endpoint evidence is reviewed.

External primary references
- Intel, “Programming Intel XMX Using SYCL Joint Matrix Extension,” which describes the joint-matrix API and XMX/DPAS operations: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/oneapi/optimization-guide-gpu/2024-1/joint-matrix.html
- Intel, “Registerization and Avoiding Register Spills,” for register pressure/spill and occupancy considerations relevant to tile/subgroup experiments: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/oneapi/optimization-guide-gpu/2023-1/registerization-and-avoiding-register-spills.html
- Intel LLVM joint-matrix extension specification (primary implementation/spec source): https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_matrix/sycl_ext_oneapi_matrix.asciidoc
- ggml/llama.cpp SYCL backend documentation, which describes its XMX gather-GEMM route for grouped MoE `MUL_MAT_ID` and its shape/token restrictions: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/backend/SYCL.md
- IntelLabs Xe-Fuse project, a primary Xe/SYCL codebase demonstrating fused GEMM epilogues and the opportunity to avoid global intermediates; it states the project is active-development/not production-ready, so it is an implementation reference, not performance validation: https://github.com/IntelLabs/Xe-Fuse
- Intel, “Optimize Your GPU Applications with the Intel oneAPI Base Toolkit,” advises tuning work-group size, avoiding register spills, minimizing tails, optimizing memory locality, and reducing redundant global memory traffic: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/training/gpu-optimization-workflow.html

Decision: source-only ranked candidates. No particular candidate is adopted and no B570 runtime backend, timing, correctness result, or speedup was measured by this audit.
